## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to design observability systems with robust tenant isolation in CNF platforms, focusing on end-to-end tracing, data segmentation, and practical implementation.

## Key Concepts
- Distributed tracing fundamentals and W3C Trace Context
- Tenant-scoped attributes and resource naming conventions
- Telemetry routing strategies (tenant-based exporters, dedicated backends)
- Sampling strategies and their impact on observability versus cost

## Code Example
```yaml
# OpenTelemetry Collector config (minimal)
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}
exporters:
  otlp/tempo:
    endpoint: tempo:4317
    headers:
      x-tenant-id: "${TENANT_ID}"
processors:
  resource:
    attributes:
      - key: tenant_id
        value: "${TENANT_ID}"
        action: upsert
  batch: {}
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [resource, batch]
      exporters: [otlp/tempo]
```

```yaml

apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-test

apiVersion: apps/v1

spec:
  replicas: 1

    metadata:
      labels:
        app: test-app

        instrumentation.opentelemetry.io/inject-sdk: "true"

        - name: TENANT_ID

```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design tenant-isolated traffic experiments, balancing fidelity with safety. Requires practical knowledge of service meshes, per-tenant config, and data privacy in production-like environments.

## Key Concepts
- Traffic shadowing with Istio or similar mesh
- Per-tenant config via NamespaceConfigMap
- Tenant selection via request header X-TENANT-ID
- Isolation: staging sink in separate trust domain
- Validation: one-namespace manifest and observability hooks

## Code Example
```yaml
# VirtualService skeleton showing mirror usage
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: VirtualService
metadata:
  name: tenant-shadow
spec:
  hosts:
  - prod-svc
  http:
  - match:
    - headers:
        x-tenant-id:
          exact: "<tenant-id>"
    route:
    - destination:
        host: prod-svc
    - weight: 100
    mirror:
      host: staging-svc
      subset: v1
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you scale per-tenant shadow percentages with burst traffic?
- How do you monitor shadow traffic to ensure no PII leakage or data exposure?
